claim: The chicken embryo has been one of the major animal models in biomedical research due to its amenability to manipulations, to live observation and its striking similarities to mammals.
source: Due to its amenability to manipulations, to live observation and its striking similarities to mammals, the chicken embryo has been one of the major animal models in biomedical research.
evidence: This is a general statement about the chicken embryo's role in research, drawing from established scientific consensus in the field.

claim: The chicken's long generation time (6 months to sexual maturity) makes it an impractical lab model and has prevented its widespread use in research.
source: Although it is technically possible to genome-edit the chicken, its long generation time (6 months to sexual maturity) makes it an impractical lab model and has prevented it widespread use in research.
evidence: This is an inference based on the practical limitations of using chicken as a model organism.

claim: The Japanese quail (Coturnix coturnix japonica) has a much shorter generation time (1.5 months) compared to chicken.
source: The Japanese quail (Coturnix coturnix japonica) is an attractive alternative, very similar to the chicken, but with the decisive asset of a much shorter generation time (1.5 months).
evidence: This is a factual statement about the generation time of Japanese quail, which is established knowledge.

claim: Most transgenic quail lines have been generated using replication-deficient lentiviruses.
source: In recent years, transgenic quail lines have been described. Most of them were generated using replication-deficient lentiviruses, a technique that presents diverse limitations.
evidence: This is a statement about the methods used to generate transgenic quail lines, drawing from established knowledge in the field.

claim: A novel technology for transgenesis in quail is based on the in vivo transfection of plasmids in circulating Primordial Germ Cells (PGCs).
source: Here, we introduce a novel technology to perform transgenesis in quail, based on the in vivo transfection of plasmids in circulating Primordial Germ Cells (PGCs).
evidence: This is the main claim of the manuscript, supported by the experimental data presented throughout the paper.

claim: The plasmid-based transgenesis technique is simple, efficient and allows using the infinite variety of genome engineering approaches developed in other models.
source: This technique is simple, efficient and allows using the infinite variety of genome engineering approaches developed in other models.
evidence: This is a claim about the properties of the technique, supported by the experimental results and comparisons made in the manuscript.

claim: The chicken embryo has been at the origin of numerous seminal discoveries in diverse topics including immunology, genetics, virology, cancer, cell biology, and ethology.
source: Due to the easy access of chicken embryos to manipulation, this model has been at the origin of numerous seminal discoveries in a diverse range of topics (e.g. immunology, genetics, virology, cancer, cell biology, ethology, etc.; Stern, 2005).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Stern, 2005.

claim: By the time the egg is laid, the chicken embryo has already developed into a blastoderm of about 40,000–50,000 cells with the germ line lineage already set aside.
source: By the time the egg is laid, the embryo has already developed into a blastoderm of about 40,000–50,000 cells with the germ line lineage already set aside (Eyal-Giladi and Kochav, 1976; Intarapat and Stern, 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Eyal-Giladi and Kochav, 1976 and Intarapat and Stern, 2013.

claim: Most researchers in avian genetics have focused their efforts on two distinct methods: the genetic manipulation of primordial germ cells (PGCs) in vitro, which are injected back into recipient embryos, or the direct infection of PGCs within the subgerminal cavity with replication-defective lentiviruses.
source: Because of this, most researchers in avian genetics have focused their efforts on two distinct methods (Nishijima and Iijima, 2013): i) the genetic manipulation of primordial germ cells (PGCs) in vitro, which are injected back into recipient embryos (Idoko-Akoh et al., 2018; Park et al., 2014; Taylor et al., 2017; van de Lavoir et al., 2006) or ii) the direct infection of PGCs within the subgerminal cavity with replication-defective lentiviruses (Bosselman et al., 1989; McGrew et al., 2004).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to relevant literature.

claim: Transgenesis in chicken is impracticable within the timeframe of most research projects due to their long generation time (6 months to sexual maturity).
source: However, due to their long generation time (6 months to sexual maturity), transgenesis in chicken is impracticable within the timeframe of most research projects.
evidence: This is an inference based on the practical constraints of research timelines.

claim: Transgenesis technology in chicken has not been widely used in basic research and its development has been mainly driven by industrial interests to produce biologically active pharmaceutical proteins in eggs.
source: Therefore, this technology has not been widely used in basic research and its development has been mainly driven by industrial interests to produce biologically active pharmaceutical proteins in eggs (Lillico et al., 2007; Nishijima and Iijima, 2013; Woodfint et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to relevant literature.

claim: Quail and chicken share on average 95% homology at the gene sequence level.
source: Indeed, quail and chicken are close relatives (Order: Galliformes; Family: Phasianidae), they share on average 95% homology at the gene sequence level (GenBank) and quails are susceptible to most chicken diseases (Barnes, 1987).
evidence: This claim is supported by reference to GenBank data.

claim: Quails are susceptible to most chicken diseases.
source: Indeed, quail and chicken are close relatives (Order: Galliformes; Family: Phasianidae), they share on average 95% homology at the gene sequence level (GenBank) and quails are susceptible to most chicken diseases (Barnes, 1987).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Barnes, 1987.

claim: Quail lay about one egg per day, similar to chicken.
source: Similar to chicken, quail lay about one egg per day, and their smaller size makes them more compatible with the frequently limited space of animal facilities.
evidence: This is established knowledge about quail reproductive biology.

claim: Quail reach sexual maturity in 6 weeks.
source: A decisive advantage of quail over chicken is that they reach sexual maturity in 6 weeks.
evidence: This is established knowledge about quail development.

claim: The life cycle of quail is significantly shorter than that of chicken (26 weeks), mice (8 weeks), or zebrafish (12 weeks).
source: Thus, their life cycle is significantly shorter than that of chicken (26 weeks), but also of mice (8 weeks) or zebrafish (12 weeks).
evidence: This is a comparison based on established knowledge about the generation times of different model organisms.

claim: No reliable technique for the culture of quail PGCs has yet been described.
source: As no reliable technique for the culture of quail PGCs has yet been described, transgenesis in this species has mainly relied on the infection of blastoderm stage embryos (or circulating Zhang et al., 2012) with lentiviruses carrying fluorescent markers under ubiquitous or tissue-specific promoters, leading in recent years to the generation of a few quail lines: ubiquitous (Huss et al., 2015; Zhang et al., 2012); neuronal (Scott and Lois, 2005; Seidl et al., 2013; adipose Ahn et al., 2015; intestinal Woodfint et al., 2017; endothelial Sato et al., 2010).
evidence: This is a statement about the current state of the field, drawing from established knowledge.

claim: A high titre of lentivirus is required to succeed at producing chimeric embryos carrying transgenic PGCs.
source: A high titre of lentivirus is required to succeed at producing chimeric embryos carrying transgenic PGCs using this technique (Poynter and Lansford, 2008; Scott and Lois, 2005).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to relevant literature.

claim: A sharp drop in viral titre is observed with inserts above 4–5 kb, likely representing the upper limit of constructs that can be used to generate transgenic birds using lentiviruses.
source: Even though large inserts (more than 10 kilobases) can theoretically be packaged using lentiviruses, a sharp drop in viral titre is observed with insert above 4–5 kb, likely representing the upper limit of constructs that can be used to generate transgenic birds (Kumar et al., 2001; our observation).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Kumar et al., 2001 and the authors' own observations.

claim: The first CRISPR/Cas9-mediated targeted gene knockout in quail was performed by direct infection of blastoderm cells using adenoviral vectors.
source: An important advance in the field was the recent use of adenoviral vectors to perform the first CRISPR/Cas9-mediated targeted gene knockout in quail by direct infection of blastoderm cells (Lee et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Lee et al., 2019.

claim: The direct in vivo transfection of PGCs with commercially available liposome-based transfection reagents has been successfully used to generate transgenic chicken lines.
source: The direct in vivo transfection of PGCs with commercially available liposome-based transfection reagents has recently been successfully used to generate transgenic chicken lines (Cooper et al., 2018b; Cooper et al., 2018a; Tyack et al., 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to relevant literature.

claim: DNA inserts up to a size of 11 kb can be cloned between Tol2 sequences with no visible loss of transposable efficiency.
source: Since DNA inserts up to a size of 11 kb can be cloned between Tol2 sequences with no visible loss of transposable efficiency (Kawakami, 2007) this allows using larger and/or more complex constructs than in viruses.
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Kawakami, 2007.

claim: Transgenesis using the Tol2 transposon system leads to minimal epigenetic silencing during development.
source: Another advantage of transgenesis using the Tol2 transposon system is that it leads to minimal epigenetic silencing during development (Macdonald et al., 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Macdonald et al., 2012.

claim: Three novel quail transgenic lines carrying fluorescent proteins under ubiquitous and tissue-specific promoters were generated using direct transfection of PGCs.
source: Here, we used the direct transfection of PGCs in the bloodstream of quail embryos. We present three novel quail transgenic lines carrying fluorescent proteins under ubiquitous and tissue-specific promoters.
evidence: This is the main result of the manuscript, supported by experimental data.

claim: A cassette containing the GFP protein driven by a promoter for Chick βB1-Crystallin makes the identification of transgenic animals possible at hatching by UV illumination.
source: Illustrating the flexibility of the plasmid-based system, we integrated a cassette containing the GFP protein driven by a promoter for Chick βB1-Crystallin (Taube et al., 2002) making the identification of transgenic animals possible at hatching by UV illumination.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data and a citation to Taube et al., 2002.

claim: Chicken PGCs initially located at the end of gastrulation within the germinal crescent enter the extra-embryonic blood vessels at about 30 hr of incubation (E1.5, HH9) and begin to circulate throughout the embryo.
source: Chicken PGCs initially located at the end of gastrulation within the germinal crescent, enter the extra-embryonic blood vessels at about 30 hr of incubation (E1.5, HH9) and begin to circulate throughout the embryo.
evidence: This is established knowledge about chicken PGC development.

claim: The number of PGCs in the blood peaks around E2/2.5 (HH15-16).
source: Their number in the blood peaks around E2/2.5 (HH15-16).
evidence: This is established knowledge about chicken PGC development.

claim: By E3 (HH20), PGCs actively migrate back in the embryo and into the gonad anlagen.
source: By E3 (HH20), PGCs actively migrate back in the embryo and into the gonad anlagen (Nakamura et al., 2007; Nieuwkoop and Sutasurya, 1979).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to relevant literature.

claim: The timing of injection of the transfection mix resulting in the colonization of fluorescent PGCs in quail is similar to that determined in chicken, at 2 days (E2) of quail embryonic development.
source: However, we found that the timing of injection of the transfection mix resulting in the colonization of fluorescent PGCs was similar to that determined in chicken, that is at 2 days (E2) of quail embryonic development.
evidence: This is a finding from the experimental work presented in the manuscript.

claim: 5 days after injection (at E7), gonads contained many fluorescent cells.
source: Indeed, 5 days after injection (at E7), we observed that gonads contained many fluorescent cells (Figure 1B).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: Fluorescent cells in the gonads were confirmed to be PGCs using whole-mount immunostaining with a PGC-specific marker VASA.
source: We confirmed that these were PGCs using whole-mount immunostaining with a PGC-specific marker VASA (Figure 1C–F).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1C-F.

claim: A 462bp-long lens-specific promoter of the βB1crystallin gene (CRYBB1) was isolated from chicken genomic DNA.
source: We isolated a 462bp-long lens-specific promoter of the βB1crystallin gene (CRYBB1; Duncan et al., 1995) from chicken genomic DNA and cloned it upstream of GFP to develop a selection mini-gene (CrystallGFP) based on lens expression.
evidence: This is a description of the experimental procedure, supported by a citation to Duncan et al., 1995.

claim: The CrystallGFP mini gene is only 1.7 kb long and can be added to transgene constructs.
source: The CrystallGFP mini gene is only 1.7 kb long and can be added to transgene constructs.
evidence: This is a factual statement about the size of the construct.

claim: Only lens cells expressed GFP when the CrystallGFP construct was co-electroporated with a ubiquitously expressed RFP into the optic cup of a quail E3 embryo, showing the specificity of the βB1crystallin promoter for lens tissues.
source: Twenty-four hours after electroporation, RFP-positive cells were found in the retina and lens (Figure 2B,D). However, only the lens cells expressed the GFP (Figure 2C,D), showing the specificity of the βB1crystallin promoter for lens tissues.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2.

claim: Transgenic quails carrying the CrystallGFP selection cassette display strong expression of GFP in all lens cells during embryogenesis and in adults.
source: Transgenic quails carrying the CrystallGFP selection cassette display strong expression of GFP in all lens cells during embryogenesis (Figure 2E–G) and in adults (Figure 2I).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2.

claim: About half of the injected eggs hatched in the transgenesis experiments.
source: In this and other experiments described below, we have observed that about half of the (50) injected eggs hatched.
evidence: This is a quantitative observation from the experimental work.

claim: Three transgenic (F1) birds could be readily spotted at hatching by fluorescence screening thanks to the ubiquitously expressed GFP and mCherry.
source: From these crosses, three transgenic (F1) birds could be readily spotted at hatching by fluorescence screening thanks to the ubiquitously expressed GFP and mCherry.
evidence: This is a finding from the experimental work.

claim: About 1% of the offspring contain the transgene, an efficiency comparable to that observed in the chicken using the same technology.
source: From this and other crosses we have performed in the laboratory (see below), we estimate that about 1% of the offspring contain the transgene, an efficiency comparable to that observed in the chicken using the same technology (Tyack et al., 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data and a citation to Tyack et al., 2013.

claim: The membrane-bound GFP results in better resolution of cell membrane processes (protrusions, filopodia, etc.) than a cytoplasmic counterpart.
source: Indeed, we observed that the membrane-bound GFP results in a better resolution of cell membrane processes (protrusions, filopodia, etc.) than a cytoplasmic counterpart, while it also combines a nuclear mCherry, allowing accurate segmentation of cells necessary for automated image analyses such as for 3D cell tracking.
evidence: This is an observation from the experimental work.

claim: Kaede undergoes irreversible photoconversion from green to red fluorescence upon irradiation with ultraviolet light.
source: Upon irradiation with ultraviolet light, Kaede undergoes irreversible photoconversion from green to red fluorescence.
evidence: This is established knowledge about the properties of Kaede protein.

claim: Three F1 founders of the TgT2(CAG:Kaede) line were obtained in which strong and ubiquitous expression of the photoconvertible fluorescent protein is observed in adult and in developing embryos.
source: Three F1 founders were obtained in which strong and ubiquitous expression of the photoconvertible fluorescent protein is observed in adult (Figure 3A) and in developing embryos (Figure 3B).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3.

claim: The long half-life of the photoconverted Kaede results in red fluorescence that can be detected up to 48 hr after photoconversion.
source: The long half-life of the photoconverted Kaede results in red fluorescence that can be detected up to 48 hr after photoconversion (Tomura et al., 2008).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Tomura et al., 2008.

claim: The TgT2(CAG:Kaede) quail line is the first avian line carrying a photoconvertible fluorescent protein.
source: This quail line is the first avian line carrying a photoconvertible fluorescent protein and it should be extremely useful to perform short to medium-term lineage tracing of cells as development proceeds.
evidence: This is a claim about the novelty of the line, based on the authors' knowledge of the field.

claim: A muscle-specific promoter was designed based on a synthetic reporter derived from the MLC1F/3F gene regulatory sequences previously utilized for mouse transgenesis.
source: We designed a muscle-specific promoter, based on a synthetic reporter derived from the MLC1F/3F gene regulatory sequences previously utilized for mouse transgenesis (3F-nlacZ-E; Kelly et al., 1995).
evidence: This is a description of the experimental design, supported by a citation to Kelly et al., 1995.

claim: The muscle-specific promoter contains a 2 kb sequence located 5' and 3' of the MLC3F transcriptional start site together with a 260 bp enhancer sequences from the 3' UTR region of the MLC3F gene.
source: It contains a 2 kb sequence located 5' and 3' of the MLC3F transcriptional start site together with a 260 bp enhancer sequences from the 3' UTR region of the MLC3F gene, necessary for the high level of transcription in muscles.
evidence: This is a description of the construct design.

claim: The MLC construct was shown to drive strong LacZ expression in all (head and body) striated muscles from the early steps of myogenesis in somites of mouse embryos throughout embryogenesis, as well as in all skeletal muscles of the foetus and in the adult.
source: This construct was shown to drive strong LacZ expression in all (head and body) striated muscles from the early steps of myogenesis in somites of mouse embryos throughout embryogenesis, as well as in all skeletal muscles of the foetus and in the adult (Kelly et al., 1995).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Kelly et al., 1995.

claim: From 242 chicks that hatched, 3 transgenic F1 founders (1 male and 2 females, that is 1.2% efficiency) were selected for the muscle-specific line.
source: F0 founder males were crossed with females and from 242 chicks that hatched, 3 transgenic F1 founders (1 male and 2 females, that is 1.2% efficiency) were selected, based on the expression of GFP in the lens (Figure 2I).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the experimental work.

claim: The GFP and RFP reporters were expressed in all (i.e. head, trunk and limb) skeletal muscles of the developing embryo in the muscle-specific line.
source: The GFP and RFP reporters were expressed in all (i.e. head, trunk and limb) skeletal muscles of the developing embryo (Figure 4I–N).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4.

claim: The first sign of mCherry expression was detected within the transition zone (TZ), where MYF5-expressing cells emanating from the medial border from the overlying dermomyotome translocate and extend along the antero-posterior axis of the embryo to form myocytes.
source: We observed that the first sign of mCherry expression was detected within the transition zone (TZ; Figure 4E–H), where MYF5-expressing cells emanating from the medial border from the overlying dermomyotome translocate and extend along the antero-posterior axis of the embryo to form myocytes (Gros et al., 2009; Gros et al., 2004; Rios et al., 2011).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4 and citations to relevant literature.

claim: MLC drives expression of the reporter genes from the early stages of myogenesis in myogenin-expressing, terminally differentiating myogenic cells within the TZ.
source: This is coherent with a recent characterization of the MLC promoter we have done using in vivo electroporation in the chicken and where we found that its activity is initiated in myogenin-expressing, terminally differentiating myogenic cells within the TZ (Sieiro et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Sieiro et al., 2019.

claim: MLC remains active in terminally differentiated myofibres, similar to what had been observed in 3F-nlacZ-E mouse embryos.
source: It remains active in terminally differentiated myofibres, similar to what had been observed in 3F-nlacZ-E mouse embryos (Kelly et al., 1995).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data and a citation to Kelly et al., 1995.

claim: In contrast to the 3F-nlacZ-E mouse line where expression of LacZ was observed in non-skeletal tissues (brain, optic vesicle and heart), the transgene was not detected in those tissues in the transgenic quails, suggesting a more rigorous restriction to the skeletal muscle lineage.
source: In contrast to this mouse line, where the expression of LacZ was observed in non-skeletal tissues (brain, optic vesicle and heart; Kelly et al., 1995), we did not detect the transgene in those tissues in the transgenic quails we analyzed, suggesting a more rigorous restriction to the skeletal muscle lineage, an observation previously made in the chicken (McGrew et al., 2010).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data and citations to Kelly et al., 1995 and McGrew et al., 2010.

claim: A website was created in which existing and future quail lines will be listed at http://quailnet.geneticsandbioinformatics.eu/.
source: To foster collaborative work in the avian community, we created a website in which existing and future quail lines will be listed (http://quailnet.geneticsandbioinformatics.eu/).
evidence: This is a factual statement about the creation of a resource.

claim: A total of 24 lines are currently listed on the website, comprising three transgenic lines generated using the transposon-based method, seven transgenic lines generated using the lentiviral-based method, 7 quail mutant lines and 7 strains obtained through breeding-selection programs.
source: Currently, a total of 24 lines are listed, comprising three transgenic lines generated using the transposon-based method (this report), seven transgenic lines generated using the lentiviral-based method (Huss et al., 2015; Moreau et al., 2019; Saadaoui et al., 2020; Sato et al., 2010; Seidl et al., 2013), 7 quail mutant lines and 7 strains obtained through breeding-selection programs (See Figure 5A–C).
evidence: This is a factual statement about the content of the website, supported by citations and Figure 5.

claim: The Quail Genome Consortium has recently obtained high quality genomic data, assembled and submitted for annotation at NCBI and Ensembl.
source: The Quail Genome Consortium has recently obtained high quality genomic data, assembled and submitted for annotation at NCBI and Ensembl (Morris et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Morris et al., 2019.

claim: Quail develop slightly faster than chicken (17–18 days for quails; 21 days for chicken).
source: Quail develop slightly faster than chicken (17–18 days for quails; 21 days for chicken).
evidence: This is established knowledge about quail and chicken development.

claim: In the lines generated, the size of the transgenic DNA constructs inserted between the two Tol2 sites ranged from 3 kb for the Kaede photoconvertible line to 7.5 kb for the MLC muscle specific line.
source: In the lines generated here, the size of the transgenic DNA constructs inserted between the two Tol2 sites ranged from 3 kb for the Kaede photoconvertible line to 7.5 kb for the MLC muscle specific line.
evidence: This is a factual statement about the constructs used in the study.

claim: A quail transgenic facility (MQTF) was recently created at Monash University, where the quail lines described in this report were established and novel technologies are being developed.
source: A significant step to promote genetic approaches in avian is the recent creation of a quail transgenic facility (MQTF) at Monash University, where the quail lines described in this report were established and novel technologies are being developed at present.
evidence: This is a factual statement about the creation of a facility.
